name: Judeo-Persian
confidence_why: Nothing read describes word stress in Judeo-Persian itself (Paul 2013, Borjian 2014, Borjian 2016, Gindin 2009, Khan 2002 and Lazard 1963 are all silent), and the one remark found, Gindin's (2003) survey aside that stress is ultimate in Persian and the Jewish Iranian dialects except penultimate Judeo-Yazdi, concerns the Judeo-Median dialects rather than Judeo-Persian, so a Persian-like final-stress reading would be an inference by analogy, not a description.

catalog_quote: In other cities these phonemes are pronounced [h], ['], and [γ] respectively, as in Persian. The stress in Judeo-Yazdi is generally penultimate, as opposed to ultimate in Persian and other Jewish Iranian dialects. Yazdis pronounce Hebrew schwa as [a], while others render it [e].

new_statements.rule_in_words: By implication for Judeo-Persian (= Persian as spoken/written by Iranian Jews): word stress falls on the final syllable, as in Persian generally; only Judeo-Yazdi (and per Borjian 2014:128 probably Judeo-Kermani, both Judeo-Median, not jude1257) deviates with penultimate stress.
new_statements.exceptions: None for Persian/Judeo-Persian; the sentence itself is about the Yazdi exception among Jewish Iranian dialects. No discussion of unstressed clitics/izafa etc. (Borjian 2016:264 mentions the unstressed izafa 'in all forms of Persian' only in passing).
new_statements.domain_note: Survey-level aside, not a description of Judeo-Persian specifically; no domain (word vs phrase) specified. The primary grammar of the languoid (Paul 2013, Early Judaeo-Persian, a written 8th-13th c. corpus) has no stress section in its TOC, and stress is not recoverable from the consonantal Hebrew-script texts.
new_statements.identity_note: jude1257 'Judeo-Persian' covers (a) Early Judaeo-Persian, the 8th-13th c. Hebrew-script written corpus described by Paul 2013, and (b) later literary JP / the Persian spoken by Iranian Jews, which the sources treat as (colloquial) New Persian. The quoted sentence is a general claim about 'Persian and other Jewish Iranian dialects'; its named exception, Judeo-Yazdi (and Kermani), belongs to Judeo-Median (Central Plateau, NW Iranian; Glottolog under Central Iran/Yazdi-Kermani varieties), not to jude1257. Bukhari (bukh1238), Judeo-Tat (jude1256) and Judeo-Shirazi are separate languoids.
